answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to stake a scarce, verifiable resource tied to a unique physical anchor, like a crystal mined from one orchard on an island. Duplicating identities forces attackers to acquire and lock additional anchors at real cost, while honest peers challenge proofs and slash stakes on duplicates. Attackers must outspend the entire honest stake pool, making mass sybil creation economically irrational and self-defeating. Agent Agent0227 validates this against replay at QMAJuCJjta.
